blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Ghosting artifacts are an open problem for popular multi-shot based high dynamic range (HDR) imaging. An effective solution is to capture two large-exposure-ratio (LER) standard dynamic range (SDR) images simultaneously via a single-shot. Brightness order reversal (BOR) artifacts are generated when the two LER images are directly fused together. It is crucial to interpolate an image with an exposure time in between the exposure times of two LER images. In this paper, a novel physics-guided diffusion model based exposure interpolation algorithm is proposed to address the BOR artifacts. An initial image is interpolated by a physics-driven component, and the residual high-frequency details are generated by a new diffusion model based component. The new diffusion model is based on the correlation analysis of generative models and includes a new predicted target to reduce the variation of the Pearson correlation between the noisy data and the target, as well as the amplification factor of the fitting error. Compared with existing neural augmented exposure interpolation algorithms on top of convolution neural networks, the proposed exposure interpolation algorithm has an inherent advantage to generate more high frequency information. Experiment results validate the proposed exposure interpolation algorithm.
blocks.zh: 幽灵文物对于受欢迎的多镜头高动态范围(HDR)成像来说是一个公开的问题. 一个有效的解决方案是通过一发一发同时捕获出两个大曝光-鼠标(LER)标准动态范围(SDR)图像. 亮度令倒置(BOR)文物在两个LER图像被直接融合在一起时生成. 至关重要的是,在两个LER图像的曝光时间之间将一个图像与曝光时间相插。 在本文中,提出了一个基于曝光插入算法的新型物理导传播模型,以解决BOR文物问题. 初始图像由物理驱动组件插出,剩余高频细节由以新的扩散模型为基础的组件生成. 新的扩散模型以基因模型的关联性分析为基础,并包括了一个新的预测目标来降低吵吵的数据与目标之间的皮尔逊关联的变异,以及适配出错的放大因子. 相较于现有神经增生的接触内插算法上于同分神经网络之上,所拟议的接触内插算法具有产生更高频信息的内在优势. 实验结果验证了拟议的曝光内插算法.

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en: Many real-world scenes are with high dynamic ranges (HDRs) while a standard dynamic range (SDR) image by an existing camera can only capture limited dynamic range of these real-world scenes. Fine details in highlight/shadow regions of these scenes cannot be captured simultaneously by the existing camera via a single-shot. There are over-exposed/under-exposed regions in an SDR image captured by the existing camera, and the saturation could affect subsequent tasks such as image classification, object detection, image segmentation, etc. An effective solution is to capture multiple SDR images with different exposures for an HDR scene [ 1 ] . The differently exposed SDR images are usually captured sequentially by multiple shots. Both camera movements and moving objects are issues for such an HDR imaging system. It is not difficult to address the former while ghosting artifacts caused by the moving objects is an open problem for multi-shot HDR imaging [ 2 ] even though there are many ghost removal algorithms [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 ] .
blocks.zh: 许多现实世界的场景具有高动态范围(HDRs),而由现有相机拍摄的标准动态范围(SDR)图像只能捕捉这些现实世界场景的有限动态范围. 这些场景的亮点/阴影区域的细微细节不能被现有的相机通过单镜头同时捕捉. 现有相机捕获的SDR图像中存在过度曝光/未曝光区域,饱和可能会影响后续任务,如图像分类,物体检测,图像分割等. 一个有效的解决办法是,为《人类发展报告》的场景捕捉具有不同曝光度的多个特别提款权图像[1]。 不同曝光的SDR图像通常通过多个镜头相继捕获. 相机移动和移动物体都是这种HDR成像系统的问题. 虽然有许多除鬼算法[3, 4, 5, 6, 7], 但移动物体造成的幽灵文物是多镜头HDR成像[2] 的一个公开问题。

blocks.en: Two large-exposure-ratio (LER) SDR images can be captured simultaneously by a single-shot using the special devices in [ 8 , 9 , 10 ] . Ghosting artifacts are not an issue for such single-shot HDR imaging. However, there are brightness order reversal (BOR) artifacts when the two LER images are directly fused together via conventional filter-based multi-scale exposure fusion (MEF) algorithms [ 11 , 12 , 13 ] . Many data-driven single-scale exposure fusion (SEF) algorithms are proposed to address the BOR artifacts for the fusion of two LER images [ 14 , 15 , 16 , 17 ] . Unfortunately, the data-driven SEF algorithms have a difficulty in preserving the scene depth of real-world HDR scene in the fused image. An alternative solution is to interpolate an image with an exposure time in between the two LER images [ 18 ] and fuse the two LER images and interpolation image using a conventional filter based MEF algorithm or a data-driven MEF algorithm. It is thus highly demanded to develop an efficient exposure interpolation algorithm.
blocks.zh: 使用[8,9,10]中的特殊装置,可以同时用单发镜头捕获两个大曝光-ratio(LER)SDR图像. 这种单拍的《人类发展报告》的成像并不涉及幽灵文物。 然而,当两个LER图像通过传统的基于滤波的多尺度曝光聚变算法直接融合在一起时,有亮度顺序反转(BOR)文物[11,12,13]. 许多数据驱动的单级曝光聚变(SEF)算法被提议用于处理BOR文物,用于两个LER图像的聚变[14,15,16,17]. 不幸的是,数据驱动的SEF算法很难在熔化图像中保存真实世界HDR场景的场景深度. 另一种解决办法是在两个LER图像[18]之间插入一个带有曝光时间的图像,并利用传统的基于MEF的滤波器算法或数据驱动的MEF算法,将两个LER图像和插图图像引信. 因此,非常需要开发高效的曝光插值算法。

blocks.en: In this paper, a novel exposure interpolation algorithm is proposed through seamless integration of physics-driven and generative AI-based methods. Similar to [ 19 , 20 ] , an image is first interpolated from the two LER images using a physics-driven exposure interpolation component. The image is then refined via a generative AI-based component which is different from the data-driven components in [ 19 , 20 ] . Our generative AI-based component has a potential to generate more high-frequency information than the the data-driven components in [ 19 , 20 ] . Instead of directly using exiting diffusion models [ 21 , 22 , 23 , 24 , 25 , 26 , 27 , 28 ] , a new diffusion model is proposed on top of theoretical analysis results in [ 29 ] . Each diffusion model has a forward process and a reverse process. The forward process begins with a ground truth data sample and evolves to a noise sample by progressively adding the Gaussian noise to the data sample. A predicted target can be defined in the forward process. A neural network is trained to map the noisy data to the predicted target during the forward process. The reverse process starts from the noise sample and converts it back to the corresponding data sample through progressively reducing the Gaussian noise from the noisy data. The noisy data and the output of the neural network at the current moment are utilized to estimate the ground-truth data and the Gaussian noise in the reverse process. They are adopted to predict the noisy data at the next moment. The reverse process is usually conducted via tens to thousands steps. Fortunately, the sampling process can be optimized using trajectory distillation [ 23 ] . On the other hand, the fitting error of the neural network could be amplified during the trajectory distillation [ 23 ] . In addition to the well known amplification factor on the fitting error of the neural network, theoretical analysis in [ 29 ] indicates that the variation of the Pearson correlation between the noisy data and the predicted target is also important to reduce the overall fitting error. Therefore, the predicted target plays an important role in the diffusion model. A new predicted target is proposed in this paper to reduce the variation of the Pearson correlation between the predicted target and the noise data as well as the amplification factor of the fitting error. The new predicted target outperforms the predicted target in [ 30 ] . A new diffusion model is then built up using the new predicted target. Finally, the new model is adopted to design a novel physics-guided diffusion model based exposure interpolation algorithm for HDR imaging. Experiment results show that the proposed exposure interpolation algorithm outperforms the exposure interpolation algorithms in [ 18 , 19 , 20 ] . Overall, the main contributions of this paper are:

blocks.en: Experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed exposure interpolation algorithm. The HDR imaging datasets introduced in [ 19 , 10 ] are adopted for training and evaluation. Specifically, the dataset is divided into three subsets, including 420 sequences for training, 40 sequences for validation, and 60 sequences for testing. To ensure data consistency, camera motion and object movement are strictly controlled, and sequences containing noticeable misalignment are excluded.Data In addition, all images are randomly cropped into patches of size 512 × 512 512\times 512 to augment the training data and improve model generalization. Furthermore, the dataset from [ 34 ] is utilized solely for testing to evaluate the network’s performance, with no involvement in the training stage. During training, the batch size is set to 4 4 . We adopt Swin-UNet [ 32 ] as the backbone network. The initial learning rate is 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5} , which is gradually decreased following a cosine annealing schedule. All experiments are implemented in PyTorch and conducted on an NVIDIA A6000 GPU.

blocks.en: Physics-driven exposure interpolation component plays an important role in the proposed neural augmented framework. Therefore, in this subsection, we first conduct a comparative evaluation of the adopted physics-driven exposure interpolation component against two representative physics-driven exposure interpolation methods reported in [ 18 , 19 ] . As summarized in Table II , the adopted physics-driven component consistently outperforms the competing approaches across multiple widely adopted image quality metrics, including full-reference metrics such as SSIM [ 35 ] , PSNR, FSIM [ 36 ] , and LPIPS [ 37 ] , as well as no-reference metrics, including CLIP-IQA [ 38 ] , Entropy, MUSIQ [ 39 ] , and HyperIQA [ 40 ] . The interpolated images by our adopted component also approach closer to the ground truth images subjectively as demonstrated in Fig. 3 . The results of the interpolation methods reported in [ 18 , 19 ] exhibit noticeable color deviation, with a bluish cast in the pavement and building regions of the first scene and washed-out, desaturated skies in the second. In contrast, our result preserves natural color tones and fine textures such as cloud structures and tile patterns, and is closest to the ground truth

blocks.en: V-F Application of Exposure Interpolation to Exposure Fusion
blocks.zh: V-F 接触的内在应用

blocks.en:
To verify the effectiveness of the proposed exposure interpolation, the virtual image Z ^ 4 \hat{Z}_{4} and the two LER images Z 1 Z_{1} and Z 7 Z_{7} are fused together using GGIF [ 41 ] . The resultant MEF algorithm is compared with GGIF [ 41 ] , MSF [ 18 ] , DeepFuse [ 14 ] , MEFNET [ 42 ] , UltraFusion [ 7 ] , and DiFuser [ 43 ] .
The GGIF, DeepFuse, MEFNET, UltraFusion, and DiFuser take the two LER images Z 1 Z_{1} and Z 7 Z_{7} as their inputs. All seven algorithms are first objectively compared. The MEF-SSIM [ 45 ] for each HDR scene is calculated using the fused image Z F Z_{F} and the set { Z 1 , Z 2 , Z 3 , Z 4 , Z 5 , Z 6 , Z 7 } \{Z_{1},Z_{2},Z_{3},Z_{4},Z_{5},Z_{6},Z_{7}\} . An HDR image is synthesized from the set { Z 1 , Z 2 , Z 3 , Z 4 , Z 5 , Z 6 , Z 7 } \{Z_{1},Z_{2},Z_{3},Z_{4},Z_{5},Z_{6},Z_{7}\} using the algorithm in [ 1 ] . The TQMI is calculated using the HDR image and the fused image Z F Z_{F} . As such, MEF-SSIM [ 45 ] and TQMI [ 46 ] measure the similarity between the fused image Z F Z_{F} and the real world HDR scene. Since ground truth sRGB images are available for the data set in [ 34 ] , the seven algorithms are also compared using PSNR and SSIM. It should be pointed out that the ground truth image is obtained by fusing all the images in the set { Z 1 , Z 2 , Z 3 , Z 4 , Z 5 , Z 6 , Z 7 } \{Z_{1},Z_{2},Z_{3},Z_{4},Z_{5},Z_{6},Z_{7}\} . This implies that PSNR and SSIM also measure the similarity between the fused image Z F Z_{F} and the HDR scene. As demonstrated in Table V , the resultant MEF algorithm by the proposed exposure interpolation algorithm outperforms the other six exposure fusion algorithms from the MEF-SSIM, TMQI, SSIM and PSNR points of view. The consistent improvements across both datasets indicate that the proposed exposure interpolation can provide useful intermediate-exposure information beyond the two original LER inputs, thereby facilitating the generation of fused images with improved structural fidelity. This experiments further demonstrate the practical value of integrating exposure interpolation into an existing fusion framework.

blocks.zh: 六 结论

blocks.en:
This paper has presented a novel neural augmented exposure interpolation algorithm
for dual large-exposure-ratio (LER) standard dynamic range (SDR) images from a high dynamic range (HDR) real world scene. A physics-driven component first
interpolated an initial image, and a new diffusion model based component then
generates the residual high-frequency details. In the proposed diffusion model, a new predicted target is designed to reduce both the variation of the Pearson correlation between the noisy data and the target and the amplification factor of the fitting error.
The proposed exposure interpolation algorithm outperforms existing exposure interpolation algorithms, with particularly clear gains in
perceptual metrics such as MUSIQ, and recovers sharper textures in highlight
regions. When the proposed exposure interpolation algorithm is integrated with an existing filter based multi-scale exposure fusion (MEF) algorithm, the resultant MEF algorithm outperform six state-of-the-art exposure fusion algorithms. On the other hand, the speed of our exposure interpolation algorithm is an issue. Future work will focus
on reducing the sampling cost of the reverse process.
